name: Tobacco smoking changes theophylline clearance
actions: Record current tobacco smoking and any recent change in smoking status.
Measure serum theophylline concentrations and reassess dosing when smoking starts or stops; cessation can raise concentrations.

rationale: Tobacco smoke induces theophylline clearance; nicotine gum does not reproduce this effect.
Stopping smoking reduces clearance and can raise theophylline concentrations.

explanation_template: Tobacco smoke increases theophylline clearance. If smoking stops, clearance can fall and theophylline exposure can rise; smoking status and serum levels matter.

references.source: DailyMed, Theophylline Solution, Smokers and Cessation of Smoking
references.citation: Smoking increases theophylline clearance; cessation reduces it and requires concentration monitoring. Nicotine gum does not affect clearance.
